title: Betty Botter
subtitle: Stops B & T
description: This exercise targets the /b/ and /t/ plosive sounds, training clear articulation of voiced and voiceless stops. The alternating pattern between B and T sharpens muscle memory for both sounds.
tip: Feel the difference: /b/ is voiced — your throat vibrates — while /t/ is voiceless. Place a finger on your throat to notice the buzz switching on and off.
phrases: But she said the butter's bitter.
If I put it in my batter, it will make my batter bitter.
But a bit of better butter, that would make my batter better.
So Betty Botter bought a bit of better butter to make her bitter batter better.
